subject: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ follow-up with PulseHealth
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ follow-up

Maya — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick written recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can align on a pilot: 

Recap from call:
- PulseHealth target workload: conversational triage + summarization for clinical notes (avg. 750 tokens/request; heavy tail up to 6k). Estimated monthly tokens: 120M–220M depending on rollout speed.
- Key must-haves: SOC2 attestation, regional hosting (US), predictable unit costs (we discussed $/1M token targets).
- Current host spend: you mentioned paying OpenAI for production chat; we'll capture more exact historic $/1M in the questionnaire.

Pricing & unit-econ ask (from call):
- PulseHealth target effective price: ~$7/1M tokens (goal) with room to tier down with committed volumes.
- Acceptable pilot pricing band: $7–$9/1M for an initial 3-month evaluation.

What I attached: PulseHealth_Questionnaire.pdf (please fill any missing historic spend lines) and a preliminary Redwood pricing grid (redwood_pricing_grid_1M.xlsx) so you can see published host comparisons and our common pilot structures.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm target $/1M (band) and preferred contract owner (procurement contact).
2) Redwood to return a pilot proposal (pricing + SLOs + SOC2 evidence) — target delivery by EOD Wed 4/14.
3) If acceptable, we run a 3-month pilot with a volume-commit addendum to secure lower tiers.

If helpful I can loop in our pricing lead (Ben) to propose a concrete playbook for caching/batching and expected effective unit economics given your 750-token average.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: PulseHealth_Questionnaire.pdf, redwood_pricing_grid_1M.xlsx
From: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@pulsehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ follow-up

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the recap and the materials. Quick answers from our side: 

- Confirmed monthly token estimate: planning exercise shows 150M tokens/month in steady state (first 3 months will be ramping: ~40M → 100M → 150M).
- Our current blended spend (production + dev): roughly equivalent to $18/1M tokens with OpenAI for chat usage (we have some Anthropic tests at ~$15/1M and experimental self-hosted runs that average ~$9/1M but with more operational overhead).
- Target: we want to get to ~$7/1M effective if possible — that would make the economics work for our pricing model. We understand that will likely require some commitments and optimizations (caching, batching, possibly quantized models).

Procurement contact: Tom Ellis (t.ellis@pulsehealth.com). He owns vendor onboarding and budget sign-off. He’s cc’d.

SOC2 is a hard requirement for go-live. We’ll need the attestation and evidence before production onboarding.

Happy for you to loop in Ben — if Redwood can show a credible path from current spend to ~$7/1M given our load profile, we’ll prioritize the pilot.

—Maya
Maya Johnson
Head of Product, PulseHealth
maya.johnson@pulsehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@pulsehealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ follow-up

Maya + team — great context, thanks. Quick note on how we’d model this and an initial pilot proposal: 

1) Unit-econ levers we’ll use for PulseHealth:
   - Prefix / KV cache for repetitive prompts (estimated 15–25% token reduction on triage flows).
   - Dynamic batching policy tuned to your 750-token median to improve throughput without hitting latency SLOs.
   - Quantized model family option (4-bit fp) for cost-lower tiers where accuracy is still within acceptable bounds.

2) Competitive benchmarking (examples you can reference):
   - OpenAI (your prod mix): approx. $18/1M (chat-heavy, no caching).
   - Anthropic (Claude-like workloads): approx. $15/1M for similar throughput.
   - Self-hosted/spot GPU runs (experimental): effective $7–$9/1M but with operational variability.

3) Initial pilot commercial: 
   - Duration: 3 months (non-production pilot with SLA-lite for latency/uptime).
   - Pilot price: $8/1M effective for the pilot period (applies to generated tokens).
   - Volume commit option: if PulseHealth commits to a 6-month ramp with a minimum monthly commit at 120M tokens, we can step down to $6.5/1M for committed volume and offer a reconciliation credit.
   - Deliverables: SOC2 attestation docs, a live dashboard with token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and a short optimization plan that quantifies expected cache/batching impact.

I attached a concise pilot proposal (pilot-proposal-PulseHealth.pdf) with the above and a simple amendment template for committing volume.

If that pilot price looks workable, Rachel — can you confirm the procurement cadence with Tom and a target start week? We can turn paperwork around within 5 business days once the SOW is agreed.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: pilot-proposal-PulseHealth.pdf
From: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@pulsehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing & unit-econ follow-up

Thanks Ben — that structure is promising. A couple quick asks before we finalize pilot: 

- Please include SOC2 Type II report / attestation in the documentation bundle. We need evidence for our security review.
- Can you add an example reconciliation calculation showing how caching + batching moves effective $/1M from $8 → $6.5 at 120M commit? A one-page worked example will help our CFO.
- Target pilot start: week of 5/3/2027 if paperwork is in place. Procurement (Tom) will review the pilot-proposal.pdf and the amendment; I’ll introduce the internal legal reviewer if needed.

If you can send the updated pilot packet with SOC2 links and the reconciliation example by EOD 4/14, we’ll accelerate procurement.
